title: Knedliky
subtitle: czech bread dumplings
excerpt: Knedliky are Czech bread dumplings made from a yeast dough enriched with egg and old bread. They are poached in logs, sliced, and served as the classic accompaniment to svickova, goulash, or any saucy Czech main. Makes 2 logs, serves 4 to 6.
sourceNotes: The definitive side dish of the Czech kitchen, appearing alongside nearly every braised meat and sauce-heavy main course.

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice cooled dumplings and freeze layered with baking paper. Reheat by steaming or pan-frying in butter.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze slices. Leftover slices are excellent pan-fried in butter.

glossaryTerms.definition: To cook food gently in simmering liquid below boiling point. Knedliky logs are poached in barely simmering water to keep them light.
To allow a yeast dough to rest and rise so the yeast ferments and produces carbon dioxide, making the dough light and airy.

content.text: for an hour before shaping into logs that are then
in barely simmering water until cooked through. They are then sliced thickly and served to soak up sauce. Makes 2 logs, serves 4 to 6.
Day-old white bread gives the best texture. Fresh bread makes the dumplings too dense.

items.prepNote: from stale white bread, not fine dust

content.text: Combine the flour, stale breadcrumbs, eggs, melted butter, and warm water in a large bowl. Mix until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest in a warm place for 1 hour until puffed.
Divide the dough into two equal pieces. Shape each into a smooth log about 6cm in diameter. Wet your hands to prevent sticking.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil. Carefully lower in the dumpling logs. Poach for 20 minutes, turning gently halfway through.
To test, pierce with a skewer. It should come out clean with no raw dough. If the inside looks wet, cook for 5 more minutes.

Remove from the water and immediately prick all over with a fork or skewer. This releases steam and prevents a soggy interior. Slice into 2cm rounds and serve immediately, or pan-fry leftover slices in butter until golden.
The dough needs a full hour to rest. Do not skip the proving time. The bread also helps the texture; use stale bread with a coarser crumb.

attrs.problem: Dumplings fall apart in the water

content.text: The water was boiling too vigorously. Keep it at a gentle simmer. The logs also need to hold their shape firmly before going in; if the dough is very loose, add a little more flour.

attrs.problem: Centre is still raw after 20 minutes

content.text: The log was too thick. Shape to 6cm diameter, not wider. Continue simmering until a skewer comes out clean.

Knedliky are as central to Czech cooking as pasta is to Italian. They appear on every traditional restaurant menu and every family table on Sunday. Their job is to soak up the sauce from svickova, goulash, or roast duck. Leftover slices fried in butter with fried egg are a popular next-day meal.
